title: SURGELLM: Rethinking Multi-Task Evaluation through Task-Aware Feature Gating with Class-Balanced Normalization
abstract: arXiv:2606.24259v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Fine-tuned encoders deployed across heterogeneous NLP tasks face three compounding problems: mismatched inductive biases, class-imbalance corruption of feature statistics, and no mechanism to condition attention on external lexical knowledge. We introduce \textbf{\surgellm}, a unified transformer framework that addresses each with a dedicated lightweight module: a \emph{surgical feature gate} (learned per-dimension sigmoid over curated lexical indicators and \texttt{[CLS]}; provably degenerates to identity when features are uninformative), \emph{task-conditioned prefix tokens} (quantized feature values and task identity prepended to every input), and \emph{Instance-Weighted Normalization} (IWN; removes class-prior bias from gate statistics). We prove an excess-risk bound linking gate benefit to \emph{surgical feature alignment}. Across four tasks, SST-2, multi-hop retrieval, LLM-prompt attribution, and authorship detection, cov

translated_title: SURGELLM：通过任务感知特征门控与类平衡归一化重新思考多任务评估
translated_abstract: 部署于异构NLP任务上的微调编码器面临三个相互叠加的问题：归纳偏置不匹配、特征统计被类别不平衡破坏，以及缺乏将注意力条件化于外部词汇知识的机制。我们提出了SURGELLM，一个统一的Transformer框架，通过专用轻量级模块逐一解决这些问题：外科手术式特征门控（surgical feature gate，对精选词汇指标和[CLS]学习逐维度的sigmoid，当特征无信息时可证明退化为恒等映射）、任务条件化前缀令牌（task-conditioned prefix tokens，将量化特征值和任务身份添加到每个输入的前面），以及实例加权归一化（Instance-Weighted Normalization，IWN，从门控统计中消除类别先验偏差）。我们证明了一个超额风险界，将门控收益与外科手术式特征对齐联系起来。在四个任务上——SST-2、多跳检索、LLM提示归因和作者身份检测……
tldr: SURGELLM提出一个统一Transformer框架，通过外科手术式特征门控、任务条件化前缀令牌和实例加权归一化三个轻量级模块，解决多任务编码器中归纳偏置不匹配、类别不平衡和外部词汇知识缺失三大问题，并从理论上证明了超额风险界。
en_tdlr: SURGELLM is a unified transformer framework that addresses mismatched inductive biases, class-imbalance corruption, and missing lexical conditioning via a surgical feature gate, task-conditioned prefix tokens, and Instance-Weighted Normalization, backed by a proven excess-risk bound linking gate benefit to surgical feature alignment.
